questions.question_text: Why does a heavy wooden log float on water while a small iron nail sinks?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Flotation depends on density (mass/volume), not total mass. Wood density is lower than water density (floats); iron density is higher than water density (sinks).

questions.question_text: Explain three methods to increase the rate of dissolving a solid solute in liquid.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Stirring/Agitation: Spreads solute particles through solvent. 2. Heating: Raises solvent kinetic energy and collision rate. 3. Powdering Solute: Increases surface area exposed to solvent.

sections.section_name: Section C (Long Answer & Case Study Questions)

questions.question_text: Describe how to determine the density of an irregular stone using a balance and graduated cylinder.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Mass Measurement: Measure stone mass (m in grams) using a beam balance. 2. Volume Measurement: Fill a graduated cylinder with water to initial volume V1. Submerge stone completely and record final volume V2. Stone volume V = V2 - V1 in cm^3. 3. Calculation: Density d = m / V g/cm^3. 4. Flotation Prediction: If d > 1.0 g/cm^3, stone sinks; if d < 1.0 g/cm^3, stone floats.

questions.question_text: Explain the principle of 9.2 Density, Volume Displacement, and Flotation and state its scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Density is mass per unit volume (d = m/V). Volume of irregular solids is measured via liquid displacement in graduated cylinders. Objects float if density < liquid density and sink if greater. [Practical Measurement: Displacement Method] Submerging an irregular object raises liquid volume by an amount equal to object volume.

questions.question_text: Explain the principle of 9.1 Components and Concentration of Solutions and state its scientific significance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: A solution consists of solute (dissolved substance) and solvent (dissolving medium). Saturation occurs when no additional solute dissolves at a given temperature. Solid solubility increases with heating; gas solubility decreases with heating. [Think like a scientist: Gas Solubility and Aquatic Life] Dissolved oxygen in water enables aquatic respiration. Warm water holds less oxygen than cold water.
